item.title: “It Will Be Their Ultimate Downfall”: Fans React As NFL Insider Reports Cam Ward Has Titans’ Full Trust
item.description: Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward (1) walks off the field post game against the Seattle Seahawks at Nissan Stadium. © Reuters The Tennessee Titans are having one of the worst seasons in their history. At 1-6, they’re off to their worst start to a season in nearly 20 years. Cam Ward’s Titans have struggled on both offense and defense, and they have been unfortunate with injuries. Ward has also had a troubling start. He has been criticized for his efficiency and decision-making all season. In seven games, he has thrown for 1,179 passing yards with four touchdowns and five interceptions. There have been rumors of the Titans looking to go away from Ward, especially after defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons’ trade to the Chicago Bears. But NFL insider Adam Schefter reported that the Titans will continue to back Ward despite a 1-6 start. Fans reacted to Schefter’s comments. “It will be their ultimate downfall. They are not a QB developing team, or they make bad picks with high draft choices. Vince Young, Jake Locker, Will Levis, now it’s Cam Ward!” one fan said . “The Tennessee Titans continue to stand squarely behind Cam Ward, and they still believe in him,” Schefter said . GM Mike Borgonzi comments about Cam Ward’s future after Jeffery Simmons trade The Titans traded Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears, the team announced on Thursday. The Bears received Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round draft pick, while the Titans received a 2027 first-round and fourth-round draft pick and a 2028 first-round pick. After the trade, speculation suggested that Cam Ward might also be on his way out. Titans general manager Mike Borgonzi commented on whether Simmons’ trade sends any message for Ward’s future. “No, I think the message is we have to get better as a team. Fifty-three guys on the roster know that we have to be better this year, the year after, and this draft capital will give us the opportunity,” Borgonzi said . item.title: St. John’s men’s basketball planning recruiting visit for four-star recruit Godson Okokoh
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - OCTOBER 14: Head Coach Rick Pitino of the St. John's Red Storm during the second half of a college basketball exhibition game against the Drexel Dragons at Carnesecca Arena on October 14, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Porter Binks/Getty Images) | Getty Images After years of almost entirely focusing on the transfer portal, Rick Pitino is intensifying his efforts on the high school recruiting trail, and another class of 2027 prospect is landing on the Red Storm’s radar. Four-star Canadian recruit Godson Okokoh is reportedly scheduling a visit to St. John’s on November 6 and 7, according to LeagueReady’s Sam Kayser. It is unclear whether Okokoh will attend the Red Storm’s matchup against Iona at Madison Square Garden on Sunday, November 8. The 6-foot-8 forward from Ottawa is the 111th-ranked prospect in his class according to 247Sports’ composite rankings and will compete in this year’s Overtime Elite season with Bella Vista Prep, who will play as the City Reapers in the league. He flashed his rim protection and inside scoring in the Nike EYBL Scholastic division and the Under Armour Circuit last season, and also made a strong impression at this summer’s NBPA Top 100 camp. One of Canada’s finest @Godson_oo was a joy to watch and super talented!! pic.twitter.com/p6r5WS2u8H — Bradley Beal Elite (@BradBealElite) September 21, 2026 Okokoh made only one other visit this year at West Virginia on October 6. His offers include Kansas, Ohio State, USC, Oklahoma State, Missouri, Creighton, Georgia Tech, Cincinnati, and Arizona State. Earlier this year, Okokoh helped Canada pull off a shocking upset over the United States to win its first-ever FIBA U18 AmeriCup gold medal. He averaged 9.0 points and 5.4 rebounds over five games and recorded a team-high eight boards in the championship final. Okokoh will be the second high school prospect to visit St. John’s this fall. Last week, five-star recruit Malachi Jordan completed a campus trip and attended the Red Storm’s dominant 87-74 win over Texas in their preseason finale. St. John’s is preparing for their season opener in the meantime, as they face Monmouth on Monday, November 2 at Carnesecca Arena (6:30 p.m., ESPN+).

item.title: “I Didn’t Live Up to the Standards”: Brian Kelly Makes Honest Admission About Getting Fired by LSU
item.description: LSU Tigers © Instagram/lsufootball Brian Kelly came into Baton Rouge with one objective in mind: win a national championship. He never managed to achieve the objective, not even reaching the College Football Playoff once during his four seasons with the LSU Tigers. Kelly had told the press that he left Notre Dame for LSU because he believed he couldn’t win a national title with the Fighting Irish. On Thursday, he admitted that he was never able to play up to the standard set for him in Baton Rouge. Speaking with Front Office Sports, the former LSU coach said: “I didn’t live up to the standards that are set there at LSU. They brought me in to win a national championship, and there was a lot of work that needed to be done to get there, more so than many thought, but at the end of the day I didn’t get to that level of expectation that they had,” Kelly said . He also said that he expects Lane Kiffin to be held to the same standard he was under when he was LSU’s coach. So far, 2026 has looked similar to the years under Kelly, with highlights and low points for the No. 15 Tigers (6-2) as their CFP hopes have only a thin margin for error. Lane Kiffin on what it means to be LSU’s coach This week, on “The Brandon Walker College Football Show,” Lane Kiffin was asked whether the thought had crossed his mind that he made the wrong choice by deciding to leave Ole Miss and whether he made the right choice when he left. It seems he’s not one for overthinking his choices: “I’ve never thought twice about this decision,” Kiffin said . He then spoke about what it means to be the coach of the LSU Tigers. “And even more,” Kiffin said. “From getting here and seeing when you play at home here and the stadium and the environment, and the state and the people, and how much support there is for football and then the kids in the state and how they play and how they love football.” The Tigers are theoretically still in contention, but another defeat would shatter their postseason hopes. item.title: “He’s [Steve Sarkisian] Not the Best QB Developer”: Analyst Thinks Arch Manning Should Play for Bo Nix, Dante Moore’s Ex-Coach
item.description: Texas Longhorns QB Arch Manning © (Instagram/@texasfootball) Arch Manning was considered top Heisman Trophy candidate and among the top five college players entering this season. After an impressive sophomore season in 2025, several analysts, like Joel Klatt, picked him as a preseason favorite for the 2027 NFL draft. However, Manning has had a hot-and-cold season. He has helped No. 11 Texas to a 5-2 record (3-2 SEC), but his future with Steve Sarkisian is a matter of discussion. Coming from a family with a football legacy, Manning was touted to become one of the top three NFL draft picks if not the first. Now, many believe that he should return to college next year. In fact, some even suggest that Manning should transfer to a team where he can grow more as a quarterback. Analyst Todd McShay believes that Manning should play under Kentucky’s Will Stein. “Maybe he’s (Sarkisian) not the best quarterback developer. I still think Arch can be a really good pro. … I’ve heard Georgia. I’ve heard Ole Miss. I’ve heard all different places of where he could transfer,” McShay said on Thursday . “There’s one guy that turned Bo Nix into Auburn, laughable Bo Nix, who got drafted 12th overall. There’s one guy who turned Dillon Gabriel into a third-round draft pick. There’s one guy that turned Dante Moore into, ‘It’s not working here at UCLA (to) now, we’re saying the upside’s better than him than (Fernando) Mendoza if he had come out or (if) he would have been the No. 2 overall pick.’ One guy, Will Stein. That’s what my advice would be, to explore that avenue,” he said. Bo Nix, Dillon Gabriel and Dante Moore all played under Will Stein in 2023, 2024 and 2025 respectively, when Stein was an offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach at Oregon. Stein became the head coach of the Kentucky Wildcats in December 2025. Fans react to Todd McShay’s advice to Arch Manning Fans have been divided on what Manning should do next season. Fans also talked about whether Manning’s potential addition would be a good idea for Kentucky. Injury problems are already giving the Nuggets trouble. Cam Johnson had to exit Denver’s first gam e of the season due to an ankle injury, making life difficult for a team that’s already missing sharpshooting forward Spencer Jones, whom they re-signed this past offseason. There are already quite a few red flags that should worry Nuggets fans about their team through the early goings of the season. item.title: Holy Cross football routs WCA; Graves 6 catches from breaking CT career receptions record
item.description: Holy Cross wide receiver Dae'Sean Graves on the sidelines against WCA on Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026, in Waterbury. (Kevin Roberts/Hearst Connecticut Media) WATERBURY - Holy Cross High football senior star wide receiver Dae'Sean Graves will need to wait at least one more week to claim his second state record of the season. Graves caught five passes for 113 yards, including a 46-yard touchdown, in Holy Cross' 56-8 win over WCA on Thursday night at Ray Snyder Sr. Field. The Crusaders improved to 6-1 with their sixth straight win, while the Spartans fell to 1-6. Graves' touchdown added to his state record. He has 52 touchdown receptions for his career. The UConn commit tied and broke Southington great Alex Jamele's career record for touchdown receptions last week in a 52-13 win at Crosby. Graves needs five more catches at Woodland on Friday, Nov. 6 (6:30 p.m.) to tie East Catholic great Joey Montalvo's career receptions record of 226. Six catches will give Graves the state record. item.title: Packers-Panthers Final Score: Pressure gets to Carolina’s Bryce Young
item.description: (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers are up to a 5-3 record after their Thursday Night Football win over the Carolina Panthers. The Packers won. The Milwaukee Brewers trotted around their new trophy . Kevin Harlan gave a speech at halftime on behalf of his father, who was added to the team’s ring of honor. It feels like it should be more of a joyful night for Green Bay, but their lack of a run game, which has been a season-long issue for the team, is what kept the Panthers alive with a chance to tie on the final play of the 27-19 ballgame. Despite getting Aaron Banks back at left guard, which pushed Laken Tomlinson to right guard, Green Bay’s backs weren’t able to get anything going against the NFL’s worst rush defense. On the night, the Packers’ three backs combined for 25 carries and 48 yards, just a 1.9 yards per carry average. Eventually, this team is going to need to turn the corner in the rushing game, or it’s going to cost them down the line. The game flow of tonight’s action went back and forth. Receiver Coleman Owen, who was limited to just punt return duty before tonight, fumbled the opening snap of the game, giving the Panthers a 3-0 lead. The Packers eventually rallied to go up 27-13 before Carolina drove on a long 12-play, 70-yard series that gave them an opportunity at the end. Another swing of momentum was when kicker Trey Smack, who has had his struggles as of late, missed an extra point on Green Bay’s first go-ahead drive of the game. The leading receiver for the Packers was Christian Watson, who had nine receptions for 113 yards, despite taking a trip to the hospital mid-game for a chest injury. This game had a little of everything. Defensively, the story of the game was that Green Bay was able to get pressure on Panthers quarterback Bryce Young, something they weren’t able to do to Detroit’s Jared Goff on Sunday. Young ended up taking six sacks and posting just 176 total yards on 47 dropbacks (3.7 yards per play), much lower than Jordan Love’s 288 on 41 (7.0). The Packers will have a “mini-bye” leading up to next Sunday’s matchup against the New England Patriots.

item.title: Big 12 fines UCF $100,000 over viral anti-Mormon chant during BYU game
item.description: WFTV UCF has been fined $100,000 by the Big 12 League for a viral vulgar chant some students made during last week’s football game against Brigham Young University. Students could be heard yelling “F the Mormons” loudly just before kickoff and well into the third quarter, according to one student who attended the game. “I wasn’t in the student section,” said Trevor Lawson, a senior at UCF. “I was kind of in the middle section away from it, but you could hear it.” Campus security removed several students from the stadium after the chants continued despite multiple announcements asking them to stop. “There were like six announcements, so maybe they should have reeled it back a little bit after that,” said Lawson. The clip was posted on X and went viral almost immediately, racking up more than 200,000 views since Saturday. “I think it’s unacceptable,” said Logan Hartsom, a junior at UCF. “I think when we go to a school like this, it’s full of opportunity. I don’t think it is okay to be calling out, especially the Mormon church, anything religiously affiliated.” The Big 12 League said in a statement, “The Big 12 remains committed to providing a respectful environment for student athletes, coaches and fans. Discriminatory conduct will not be tolerated.” A spokesman for UCF’s athletic department said the school is “reviewing its options” in the wake of the fine. The Packers improved to 5-3, but remained in fourth place in the ultra-competitive NFC North. The Panthers fell to 3-4 and are tied for first place in the horrendous NFC South. But Love just keeps soldiering on and should be a top-five candidate for MVP as the midway point of the season nears. Love threw three touchdown passes for the first time this season, completed 30 of 41 passes for 288 yards and posted a 106.6 rating. item.title: No. 22 Florida State defeats No. 5 Duke 2-1 in Tallahassee
item.description: No. 22 Florida State women’s soccer bounced back from Saturday’s loss to Notre Dame with a 2-1 victory over No. 5 Duke in Tallahassee. The Seminoles entered the matchup looking to respond after being shut out 2-0 by Notre Dame. Facing another ranked ACC opponent, Florida State came out strong, scoring twice in the opening 13 minutes. With the win, Florida State improved to 8-2-3, while Duke fell to 9-2-4. Florida State made several changes to its starting lineup, which included Wrianna Hudson, Shaneil Buckley, Ryder Ajeto, Sam Erbach, Peyton McGovern, Nawreen Ahmad, Tanner Strickland, Grace Hoytink, Bridget Mutipula, Janet Okeke and Kate Ockene. At 9:24, Buckley used her speed to make a run toward Duke’s goal. With the Blue Devils’ goalkeeper coming out to challenge, Buckley found an opening and scored to give the Seminoles an early 1-0 lead. Florida State continued to pressure Duke’s defense, creating another opportunity that resulted in a corner kick. At 12:47, Erbach delivered the corner kick into the box, finding Strickland in position to finish and extend the Seminoles’ lead to 2-0. Duke responded with several offensive opportunities, but Ockene kept the Blue Devils from scoring early, recording saves at 19:56 and 20:39. At 31:00, Duke’s Mia Minestrella found the back of the net after Ockene came off her line, cutting Florida State’s lead to 2-1. The Seminoles nearly extended their lead again at 33:59, but Buckley’s shot went just wide to the right. Florida State entered halftime holding a one-goal advantage over the Blue Devils. In the second half, both teams continued creating scoring opportunities as Duke looked for an equalizer. At 73:12, Ashley Henderson recorded a shot for Florida State, but Duke goalkeeper Molly Vapensky made the save. The Seminoles also put together a series of passes to maintain possession, although they were unable to turn the opportunity into another goal. At 81:32, Hudson had another chance to extend Florida State’s lead, but her shot missed to the left. Despite Duke’s efforts to even the score, Florida State held on for the 2-1 victory. Ockene finished with four saves, while both teams recorded five shots on goal. The Seminoles will travel to Coral Gables to face Miami on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 4 p.m.
